name: Bihari
bio: Bihari (Bihari Lal Chaube, 1595–1663) is the most celebrated poet of the Riti period of Braj Bhasha poetry. Tradition says he was born near Gwalior and grew up in Mathura, and that he served at the court of Mirza Raja Jai Singh of Amber (Jaipur), whom he is said to have recalled from the pleasures of a new marriage to his duties by a single couplet.

His fame rests on one book, the Satsai (the "seven hundred"), a collection of about seven hundred dohas on love, on Radha and Krishna and on the conventions of Riti poetry, packed with compressed imagery. It was edited and annotated at length by Jagannathdas Ratnakar as Bihari-Ratnakar (1926), the edition from which the verse here is taken.
